rationale_overall: Filtered out the large majority of this week's pool as noise: rolling Iran-Israel-Gulf war reporting (missile/drone strikes on UAE, Qatar, Israel, Lebanon, a sunk Iranian warship) names no investable defense-contractor ticker and reads as event journalism, not an equity catalyst; SpaceX, MatX, and TerraPower items reference private companies with no public line; INL's molten-salt facility is a government lab, not a ticker; and several AI/robotics/quantum items (whatech.com blog spam, sciencedaily quantum piece, F1-AI feature, Helena robotics students) carry no company or ticker at all. The one item with real signal - Broadcom's reported $100B AI-chip commitment (datacenterknowledge.com, 2026-03-06) - is a legitimate AI-wave catalyst but does not show any current holding (GOOGL, NVDA, RKLB, SMR) weakening or peaking this week, so it doesn't clear the bar for a swap under this week's rule (add only paired with a clearly-justified remove). Nuclear-adjacent headlines (Wyoming reactor permit, Japan-US $550B nuclear package) reinforce rather than challenge the existing SMR thesis and name no new ticker. No genuine rising-wave vehicle displaced a current holding this week; watchlist unchanged.
